figures.caption: Fig. 4: Plate Handover. Keyframes from UVT policy: the right arm Approaches and slides below the thin paper plate, Lifts it off the table, performs the dual-arm Handover, and the left arm Places it back down. The most challenging step is the initial approach, where a gripper finger must slide underneath the thin plate, and the handover stage, where both grippers have to coordinate the movement. # Half denotes half successes where gripper picks up the plate but fails the handover.

Fig. 2: Lift Pot. Keyframes from a real-world rollout of our UVT policy: both arms Reach toward the pot, Orient their grippers toward the side handles, Grasp, and Lift the pot off the table. The Grasp stage is the main bottleneck: the zoom-ins show the baseline’s dominant failure modes, an awkward grasp closing on the rim or a missed grasp missing the handles; since both handles must be secured simultaneously, either failure by either arm fails the trial. See videos on our webpage.

Fig. 3: Close Marker. Keyframes from UVT policy: the arms Reach toward the marker and cap, Orient their grippers parallel to the table, Grab the marker body and cap with separate grippers, then Align and Insert the cap onto the marker. This is the most precision-demanding task: the zoom-in panels highlight the Align steps, where sub-centimeter accuracy is required. # Half denotes half successes where grippers pick up both objects successfully but fail the insertion.

Fig. 1: Unified Visuomotor Target (UVT) Overview. Top (Extracting UVT): a frozen pretrained inverse dynamics model extracts discrete dynamics codes zt from future observations, while ground-truth action chunks at ∈ Rk×d (k: chunk size, d: action dimension) provide continuous motor supervision. Two trainable encoders map at and zt to Gaussian posteriors, which are fused via a weighted Product-of-Experts [28] with learnable precision weights αa, αz to produce the unified visuomotor target ut ∈ R32. The target is decoded to reconstruct both robot actions (LACT) and dynamics codes (LDYN), while a KL divergence loss LKL regularizes ut toward a standard normal prior, encouraging a well-conditioned prediction space. Bottom (VLA finetuning): the VLA policy is supervised to predict ut, and a trainable action decoder maps the predicted target back to executable actions, enabling faster convergence and better performance with no architectural changes and no extra data.
